evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor: t=45.8 h value 12.80 mg/L, t=46.0 h value 8.37 mg/L — abrupt ~4.5 mg/L step-down at t≈46 h
Receiving DO declines from 8.37 to 6.95 mg/L between t=46.0 and t=51.8 h; linear fit slope ≈ -0.19 mg/L/h (r²≈0.9), projecting DO≈2 mg/L near t≈78 h under KEEP
Delayed product assays: P = 1.16 g/L at t=35.8 h and 3.16 g/L at t=47.8 h — active production ongoing, so retaining feed preserves product mass

Source batches (e.g., source-1 DO dipping to ~7.4–7.9 around t≈72–74 h then recovering to >9 mg/L) show dips can be transient, but the receiving dip occurred early (t≈46 h) and is monotone-declining for ~6 h, unlike the source pattern
allowed_actions: increase_air = (1.0, 1.15) — 15% aeration increase with no feed change
args.rationale: Receiving-process DO shows an abrupt drop (~12.8 → ~8.4 mg/L) at t≈46 h followed by a persistent decline of ~0.19 mg/L/h, reaching ~6.95 mg/L by t≈51.8 h. Extrapolated under KEEP, DO reaches the 2 mg/L hard limit near t≈78 h, well inside a 96 h-type horizon, so continued KEEP risks a hard-constraint violation. A 15% aeration increase directly raises oxygen transfer capacity: since DO has settled ~7 mg/L below saturation (~14 mg/L), the transfer driving force is large, and a 15% increase in the transfer coefficient adds a supply term far exceeding the current 0.19 mg/L/h net deficit, so DO should re-stabilize comfortably above the 2 mg/L limit. Feed reduction (reduce_feed/combined/strong_feed_reduction) would also relieve oxygen demand but sacrifices product formation rate (delayed P assays show production actively rising: 0 → 1.16 → 3.16 g/L over the last two assay points), which the priorities say to retain among feasible plans. increase_air is the least invasive single action that addresses the oxygen deficit while retaining product mass. If the DO drop were caused by an aeration hardware failure (i.e., the commanded air rate is not actually delivered), the air increase could be ineffective; the DO should be watched closely and a feed reduction or stop pursued if DO keeps falling toward the limit. Stop is not warranted: current DO (~6.95 mg/L) has ample margin to 2 mg/L and a feasible operating plan is supported by evidence.
args.uncertainty: No calibrated receiving-process model is available; the projection of DO reaching 2 mg/L at ~78 h under KEEP is a linear extrapolation of a noisy sensor trend and could be optimistic or pessimistic. The effectiveness of a 15% air increase depends on whether the DO decline stems from insufficient gas transfer (which air increase addresses) versus a process-side oxygen demand spike or aeration equipment fault (which it may not). If the commanded air increase is not physically delivered, DO could continue falling and require feed reduction or stop. The simulation horizon beyond t=52 h is assumed comparable to the source batches (~96 h); a shorter horizon would reduce KEEP risk but a conservative plan is still appropriate. No guarantee of physical feasibility or safety is established.
